function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| What Turbonomic Does | Why It Matters for Unilever | How It Works |
|----------------------|-----------------------------|--------------|
| **Real‑time Resource Optimization** | Keeps workloads running at optimal performance while minimizing spend across all clouds. | Uses continuous telemetry from VMs, containers, databases, and applications to build a live “resource map.” AI models predict future demand and automatically move or resize resources. |
| **Unified Visibility Across Clouds** | Gives a single pane of glass for workloads spread over GCP, AWS, Azure, private clouds, and edge sites. | Integrates natively with each provider’s APIs (Compute Engine, ECS/EKS, AKS, etc.) plus third‑party monitoring tools (Prometheus, Datadog). All metrics, events, and policies appear in one UI. |
| **Policy‑Based Automation** | Enables business‑driven rules (e.g., “keep latency < 200 ms for e‑commerce checkout”) that span multiple clouds. | Users define high‑level policies; Turbonomic’s engine translates them into concrete actions (scale up/down, migrate, reallocate) and enforces them automatically. |
| **Cost Forecasting & Chargeback** | Provides accurate, granular cost attribution per product line or business unit—critical for Unilever’s global finance governance. | Aggregates usage data from all clouds, applies AI to forecast future spend, and generates chargeback reports aligned with internal accounting structures. |
| **Compliance & Governance** | Ensures workloads stay within regulatory boundaries (GDPR, CCPA, local data residency laws). | Continuously checks policy compliance and alerts/auto‑remediates violations before they become audit issues. |
| **Hybrid & Edge Support** | Extends observability to on‑prem, edge, and IoT devices that support Unilever’s supply‑chain analytics. | Connects via Turbonomic Agent to any environment that exposes standard metrics/APIs. |

### Key Benefits for Unilever

| Benefit | Impact |
|---------|--------|
| **Cost Savings** | AI‑driven right‑size recommendations can reduce cloud spend by 20–30 % without impacting performance. |
| **Performance Consistency** | Continuous optimization keeps SLAs met even during traffic spikes (e.g., holiday sales). |
| **Operational Agility** | Auto‑migration lets Unilever shift workloads to cheaper regions or providers in real time. |
| **Governance Confidence** | Automated compliance checks lower audit risk and free up compliance teams to focus on strategy. |
| **Strategic Decision‑Making** | Forecasting dashboards give executives clear insight into where to invest or divest. |

---

## Difference Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Provider Tools

| Feature | Turbonomic | GCP Operations Suite (formerly Stackdriver) | AWS CloudWatch | Azure Monitor |
|---------|------------|-------------------------------------------|---------------|---------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + hybrid + edge | Single‑provider (GCP) | Single‑provider (AWS) | Single‑provider (Azure) |
| **Optimization Engine** | AI/ML‑based predictive optimizer that recommends actions | Basic alerting & dashboards | Basic alerting & dashboards | Basic alerting & dashboards |
| **Automation** | Policy‑driven auto‑scale, migration, reallocation | Manual scaling via Cloud Functions or Cloud Scheduler | Manual scaling via Lambda or Step Functions | Manual scaling via Logic Apps or Automation |
| **Chargeback / Cost Attribution** | Built‑in cost modeling, forecasting, chargeback reports | Billing export + custom BigQuery queries | Cost Explorer + custom reports | Cost Management + custom dashboards |
| **Observability Depth** | Unified view of compute, storage, network, application, and business KPIs | Cloud‑native metrics + logs + traces | Cloud‑native metrics + logs + traces | Cloud‑native metrics + logs + traces |
| **Integration Flexibility** | Supports any API‑exposed metric source (Prometheus, Datadog, etc.) | Primarily GCP services | Primarily AWS services | Primarily Azure services |
| **Governance** | Policy engine that spans multiple clouds and enforces compliance | IAM roles + organization policies | IAM roles + service control policies | RBAC + Azure Policy |
| **Learning Curve** | Requires initial setup of agents and policy definition but offers guided wizards | Familiar to GCP users | Familiar to AWS users | Familiar to Azure users |
| **Use Case Fit** | Best when you have a multi‑cloud strategy and want automated, AI‑driven decisions | Good for pure GCP environments needing basic monitoring | Good for pure AWS environments needing basic monitoring | Good for pure Azure environments needing basic monitoring |

### Bottom Line

* **Native tools** provide excellent monitoring and alerting *within their own ecosystem*, but they lack cross‑cloud optimization, unified chargeback, and AI‑driven automation.
* **Turbonomic** fills that gap by giving Unilever a single platform that not only watches everything but also *acts* on the data—moving workloads, resizing resources, and ensuring compliance—all driven by AI and governed by business‑centric policies.

For a company like Unilever, whose digital footprint spans multiple continents and cloud providers, Turbonomic offers the strategic advantage of turning disparate telemetry into coordinated, cost‑effective, and compliant operations.
